answer: A new identity cannot transact until two established agents each stake a slice of their own standing to endorse it, like a walnut cracking only when two hands press together. Endorsements are scarce, each agent can sponsor just one newcomer per epoch, and if the newcomer cheats both sponsors lose standing, so sponsors vet carefully. The cost then ripples outward: a sybil farmer must win over a wide meadow of independent sponsors, paying bribes or real work for every fake identity, while an honest newcomer needs only two genuine introductions.
